title: Reporting What Others Say: The Coca Debate

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *según* + a source and reporting verbs such as *decir que* and *informar de que* from B1 Unit 13. Reporting keeps what a source says apart from what you say yourself. The coca leaf is a topic where people disagree, so it is useful to say clearly who says what.

sections.title: Who says what about coca
rows: Según la Constitución de 2009, la coca es patrimonio cultural de Bolivia.
According to the 2009 Constitution, coca is a cultural heritage of Bolivia.
El gobierno boliviano dice que la coca no es cocaína.
The Bolivian government says that coca is not cocaine.
Según Naciones Unidas, parte de la coca llega al narcotráfico.
According to the United Nations, part of the coca ends up in drug trafficking.
Los cocaleros explican que la coca tiene usos tradicionales.
The coca growers explain that coca has traditional uses.

items.spanish: El gobierno informó de que la coca se vende legalmente en algunos mercados.
items.english: The government reported that coca is sold legally in some markets.

items.spanish: Según la ley boliviana, la hoja de coca se puede usar en la vida diaria.
items.english: According to Bolivian law, the coca leaf can be used in daily life.

items.spanish: Naciones Unidas dice que el control del cultivo es importante.
items.english: The United Nations says that controlling the crop is important.

sections.content: After *decir* and *explicar* use *que*, never *de que*: *dice que*. After *informar* use *de que*: *informó de que*. Put the source first (*según…*) so the reader knows whose words they are.
